Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test `testAxisFollowing()` uses the XPath expression `//location[2]/following::node()[2]` which depends on correctly identifying any type of node with the `node()` test. The current bug report explains that the DOMNodePointer.java implementation has a method that handles node matching, but for the `node()` test it only returns true if the node is an element or a document node. Specifically, it matches only `Node.ELEMENT_NODE` or `Node.DOCUMENT_NODE` for `Compiler.NODE_TYPE_NODE`, but according to the XPath axis and node test semantics, the `node()` test should match any node type, not just elements or documents.

The exact code snippet from the report indicates at line 120, the case for `Compiler.NODE_TYPE_NODE` is:

```java
case Compiler.NODE_TYPE_NODE:
  return nodeType == Node.ELEMENT_NODE || nodeType == Node.DOCUMENT_NODE;
```

and the proposed fix is:

```java
case Compiler.NODE_TYPE_NODE:
  return true;
```

This means the code currently excludes other node types such as text nodes, comments, processing instructions, etc., from matching when using the `node()` test. This causes the XPath evaluation against the DOM model to be incorrect and likely causes the test failure in axes like `following::node()`.

None of the recent bug reports directly contradict or override this diagnosis. They mention issues in BasicNodeSet and casting problems but not this core node type matching logic.

Therefore, the root cause of the test failure is that the node test matching method in DOMNodePointer incorrectly restricts the nodes matched by the XPath `node()` test, causing incorrect axis query results such as in the following axis. The fix is to modify the matching for `Compiler.NODE_TYPE_NODE` to return true for all nodes, not just element or document nodes.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
